responseMessageContents.text:
Yes, this is fixable — the issue is **Apple Maps marker collision**. When you render 120+ markers at a world-level zoom, iOS automatically hides markers it considers visually overlapping (even if they're hundreds of km apart at that zoom). That's why Everest and others vanish. It's an Apple Maps behavior, not a bug in your data.

Here are your options:

**Option A (quickest, what I'd recommend):** Show fewer markers when zoomed out (only summited + major peaks >6000m), and reveal all peaks as the user zooms in. This keeps the map readable at every zoom.

**Option B:** Switch to Google Maps on iOS — better at handling dense markers, but requires a Google Maps API key and a native rebuild.

**Option C:** Add marker clustering (group nearby peaks into a numbered bubble). Looks great but requires a clustering library and more work.

Want me to go with Option A? I can ship it right now.
